title: Lower bound for the Gaussian Mills ratio
statement:
For every real $t<0$, the signed lower-tail Mills ratio $R(t)=\Phi(t)(-t)/\varphi(t)$ satisfies
\[
1-(t^2)^{-1}\le R(t),
\]
where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function and $\varphi$ is its density.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$, and $R(t)=\Phi(t)(-t)/\varphi(t)$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. For every real $t<0$, one has $1-t^{-2}\le R(t)$.
